# Session Coldstore
Tiered storage for DeepSeek Harness sessions.

DSH keeps every session in one live root and re-reads it on every listing, and
any full-text index b

uild has to chew through all of it. On a large corpus that
is fine on disk and expensive in memory.

Coldstore moves sessions you have not
touched in a while out of the live root — **without deleting t

hem** — and keeps
them searchable through an on-disk FTS5 index.
## What actually gets cheaper
| | Hot (live root) | Cold (`~/.dsh/coldstore`) |

| Sidebar / session list | yes | no |
| `readdir` listing scan | yes | no |
| Full-text index build

input | yes | no |
| Disk | yes | yes — nothing is deleted |
| Restorable | — | one click, or `bin/c
oldstore.mjs restore` |

Coldstore does **not** reduce a running process's heap by itself: an unopened
session's transcript w

as never resident. What it fixes is the *corpus* — the
work every listing, search and index build ha

t. What it fixes is the *corpus* — the
work every listing, search and index build has to do over it.

| key | default | meaning |

| `dryRun` | `true` | nothin

ed as opened |
| `minIdleMs` | `3600000` | minimum idle floor; a session must be idle for `max(retai

nDays, minIdleMs)` |

| `sweepIntervalMi

eze |
| `notifyOnSweep` | `true` | post a macOS notification after an automatic sweep that moved som
`notifyOnSweep` | `true` | post a macOS notification after an automatic sweep that moved something |

The Settings page writes seven of these keys to `~/.dsh/coldstore/config.json`
(`retainDays`, `dryRu

n`, `keepPinned`, `keepStarred`, `keepUnread`,
`minIdleMs`, `notifyOnSweep`), which overrides the ro

w config without touching
your patch layer. The rest are row/JSON-only. Note that `minIdleMs` is a f

loor,
not an addition: a session must be idle for `max(retainDays, minIdleMs)`.
## Exemptions
In precedence order, a session is never frozen when it is:

Nothing on this list is a soft preference: the same classifier decides a plan,
a staged commit and a

direct freeze, so naming a session explicitly does not
move it past an exemption.

**The `unread` limitation, stated plainly:** DSH keeps no durable "you read
this" marker — the "unop

ened" dot is transient client state. Coldstore keeps its
own ledger (`read.json`) from the moment it

is installed. Sessions that already
existed before installation have no read history, so they are g

overned by
`retainDays`, pin and star instead. Review the first dry-run plan and star
anything you w

anything you want protected.
## Two sweep paths
| Path | Trigger | Behaviour |
| **Manual (maker/checker)** | the Settings page | **Stage sweep** produces a reviewed batch and mov
es nothing. You then **Commit** — that moves exactly the batch you reviewed. A stale batch id is rej

ected, so a plan reviewed in one tab cannot commit a different plan staged in another. |
| **Automat
ic** | `sweepOnBoot`, `sweepIntervalMinutes` | plans and moves in one step, no checkpoint. `dryRun:
true` still blocks every move. |

At commit the Host **re-derives eligibility** and skips anything that stopped
qualifying since stagi

ng — newly pinned, starred, opened, live, or aged back
inside `retainDays`. Those skips are reported
, never silently applied.

The staged batch persists in `coldstore/pending.json`, so a page refresh keeps
showing it until you

showing it until you commit or discard.
## Notifications

An **automatic** sweep that actually moves something posts a native macOS
notification (`osascript`)

summarising what happened, for example
*"42 sessions frozen (128.4 MB) · 480 kept live"*. Boot swee

ps and interval
sweeps both do this; a sweep that moves nothing stays silent. Set
`notifyOnSweep: fa
lse` to turn it off.

This deliberately does **not** use `dsh-notify-me`. That plugin is passive and
client-side: it fires

when a session goes running→idle or asks for attention,
and it exposes no API for a plugin to post

a custom notification. A scheduled
sweep is not a session turn, so routing through it would silently

ification. A scheduled
sweep is not a session turn, so routing through it would silently never fire.

Notifications are best-effort: a missing `osascript` or a denied permission is
logged and never fail

s the sweep. The sweep also clears any staged manual batch
after it moves sessions, so the page cann

ot offer a Commit for sessions that
already left.
